clue.text: Lock on phone allowed

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them
let means allowed, as in 'let him go'

explanation.surface: A phone has been unlocked and permitted to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl of hair hanging down is called a lock, and a small corkscrew curl is the same thing.

clue.text: Party with one in list of employees

indicators.note: in says one is placed inside the list

parts.note: a roster is a list of staff and their duties
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A firm's party includes someone on the staff list.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, i.e. to celebrate wildly.

clue.text: Pictures of Trafalgar Square?

parts.note: not photographs of the square but the paintings housed on its north side

explanation.surface: Someone asks for photographs of a London landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: Trafalgar Square is in central London; the gallery of paintings stands on its north side.
explanation.definitionFit: The national art collection hangs in the building on Trafalgar Square, so its pictures are that gallery's.

clue.text: Let Munich upset one?

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters of let Munich are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A football fan wants Munich beaten in an upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one?' means one o'clock, a typical hour to eat a midday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: One o'clock is the classic hour for the midday meal.

clue.text: Attempts to determine guilt in a number of points?

definitions.meaning: courts hold hearings to decide if the accused is guilty
in rugby, grounding the ball scores five points each time

explanation.surface: Efforts to settle guilt rest on several points of argument.
explanation.walkthrough: A rugby try is a touchdown worth points.
explanation.definitionFit: A court case hears the accused; in rugby, touchdowns are scores worth points, both called by the same word.

clue.text: On river estimated time of arrival is material

indicators.note: on in an across clue says the next piece is placed after, so it follows the river

parts.note: the Taff is the river running through Cardiff in Wales

explanation.surface: A boat's arrival time on a river is announced as a matter of fact.
explanation.walkthrough: The TAFF is a Welsh river, through Cardiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp woven silk fabric, so it is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Possible description of iron opponent in temporary home

indicators.note: in says the opponent sits inside the temporary home

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
a rival is an opponent

explanation.surface: An opponent with an iron, perhaps a golfer, camps in a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: Iron can have a valency of three, as in ferric compounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferric iron combines with three other atoms' worth of bonds, so chemists call it of valency three.

clue.text: Don't succeed in holding learner's threshing implement

indicators.note: holding says the failure wraps round the learner

parts.note: to not succeed is to fail
L is the learner plate symbol; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A learner fails to master a farm tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A flail is a hinged stick used to beat grain from the husks by hand.

clue.text: Butchering deals maybe leading to a scene in Scottish capital

indicators.note: maybe says butchering deals is just one arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Bad business deals lead to an unpleasant scene in Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butchering' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'maybe' signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortress on its rock dominates the view of Scotland's capital, a famous sight there.

clue.text: A name doyen misspelt caused irritation

indicators.note: misspelt says the letters of doyen are written in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone misspelled a senior figure's name and upset them.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy someone is to irritate them, so annoyed is to have caused irritation.

clue.text: Strengthening how we count if one's taking unusual action

parts.note: the decimal system counts in tens
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for 'is', a link

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters of action are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone muses on decimal counting and what would happen if they did something odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges ACTION into CATION; 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensifying something means making it stronger, so the act of doing it is strengthening.

clue.text: Sound horn hard, seeing canine?

parts.note: to toot is to sound a horn
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A driver blasts the horn hard on seeing a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' looks like a dog but is the pointed tooth, and 'Sound' is a verb, not a homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is the pointed tooth between incisors and premolars.

clue.text: Arabs may be looked after by one son joining firm

definitions.text: Arabs may be looked after by one

parts.note: stable means firm and steady
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A son joins a company that might look after Arab clients.
explanation.walkthrough: Arabs here are horses of the Arabian breed, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad who works in horse stables tends the horses, Arabian breed included.

clue.text: A Northern Ireland team playing about, initially, bring things to life again

indicators.note: initially says the 'about' piece goes at the very start

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of team are set out in a lively new order

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish side plays a match that revives everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals the anagram and 'initially' places the 'about' word first; 'team' reads as a sports side in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To revive something is to give it life once more; the verb with re- means exactly that.

clue.text: Irregular primate reaching SA port detectives held up

parts.note: an ape is a primate
Rio de Janeiro is a South American port

indicators.note: held up in a down clue says the detectives are read from bottom to top

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British detectives

explanation.surface: A wayward ape reaches a South American port where detectives are delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aperiodic does not repeat at regular intervals, so it is irregular.

clue.text: Took centre out of company, showing embarrassment

parts.note: turning red is the colour of embarrassment

explanation.surface: Someone removed the middle of a company and blushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the core of an apple is taking its centre out.

clue.text: Queen about to hug tailless cat, with time to feed it …

indicators.note: to hug says the about piece wraps round the rest

parts.note: CA (circa) means about

indicators.note: to feed it says the time goes inside the shortened cat
tailless says the last letter of the cat is dropped

parts.note: a leopard is a big cat

explanation.surface: A queen cuddles a cat without a tail and finds time to feed it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in 'to feed it' is the cat, so the time goes inside the shortened cat before 'to hug' wraps the whole. The ellipsis links to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Egyptian ruler loved by Antony was a queen.

clue.text: Follow some obtuse guests

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to tail a few dim-witted visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: To segue is to move smoothly on to the next item, following straight from it.

clue.text: … must upset little dog, getting fork out?

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters of must are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: Someone must be upset at having to pay for a puppy.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump up is British slang for paying out, the same as forking out.

clue.text: Enter, with trepidation,

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is 'Enter, with trepidation, (9)': it ends after a comma with no definition and nothing giving CHAT; no scan or reprint found.

clue.text: Raymond follows milk supplier, source of refreshment

indicators.note: follows says the Raymond piece comes after the milk supplier

parts.note: a teat supplies milk to young animals
Ray is the short form of Raymond

explanation.surface: Raymond trails the milkman, hoping for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray carrying cups and pot brings drinks to the table.

clue.text: Peacekeepers advance, holding day one good for disembarkation

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations forces

indicators.note: holding says the loan wraps round the day and one

parts.note: an advance of money is a loan
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: UN troops advance while holding a single good day for landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advance' is a cash loan, not a troop movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Unloading a ship means getting cargo and people off it, which is disembarkation.

clue.text: One with inclination for something often dropped?

parts.note: one is the article a
an itch is a restless urge or desire

explanation.surface: Someone with an urge for a thing that is often let fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Many English speakers drop the letter H, as in ' 'ouse' for house.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H is often left unsaid at the start of words in many accents.

clue.text: Coming up to pop concert in tapered sleeve

parts.note: a gig is a pop concert

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue says the word to is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Heading off to a pop concert in fashionable sleeves.
explanation.walkthrough: GIG reads the same either way, so only TO turns, giving OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigot is a leg-of-mutton sleeve, wide at the shoulder and narrow at the wrist.

clue.text: Spanish square rebuilt in La Paz

indicators.note: rebuilt says the letters of La Paz are put together in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A town square in the Bolivian city of La Paz is reconstructed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaza is the Spanish word for a public square in a town.

clue.text: Conjuror, Italian, with possibly adroitest grip around

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters go round the Italian piece
possibly says adroitest grip is only one way the letters could be arranged

parts.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: An Italian magician has the most nimble grip of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram of the two words, and 'around' says they go round the Italian abbreviation; 'grip' reads as a magician's hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A prestidigitator performs sleight of hand, like any magician.

clue.text: Cunning spy's smart, using sixth sense?

indicators.note: cunning suggests the letters of spy are twisted craftily

parts.note: the word spy, its 's a link
chic means smart and stylish

explanation.surface: A clever spy is well dressed and seems to know everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychic claims powers beyond the five senses, that is, a sixth sense.

clue.text: Find railway's fine architectural feature

parts.note: to trace something is to find it
RY is the abbreviation for railway; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Discover a railway's fine building detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracery is the ornamental stonework in Gothic windows, a delicate building ornament.
